The record does not decide whether leadership’s authority over the recommendations defeats that stated requirement. The paper’s framework-wide conclusion and OpenAI’s comparison of Version 2 with its predecessor are context. The rule’s own wording is recorded in prov-preparedness-v2-high-deployment-restriction.

object.value: Commitment not to train or deploy without adequate safeguards

time.note: Absence recorded for this edition, dated by its effective date.

claims.inferenceRationale: Premises: RSP · v2.2 states this provision (prov-rsp-v2-2-no-train-deploy-without-safeguards). The inspected scope of RSP · v3.0 was: RSP v3.0 (effective February 24, 2026), whole text layer, PDF pp. 1–19: Introduction (pp. 3–4); §1 Our Recommendations for Industry-Wide Safety with the threshold table (pp. 4–9); §2 Frontier Safety Roadmap and §3 Risk Reports, 3.1–3.6.3 (pp. 10–15); §4 Governance (p. 15); Appendix A: Commitments Related to Competitors and Appendix B: Notes on ASLs (p. 16); Changelog (pp. 17–19).. Method: Read every section and compared it with the v2.2 provision (Executive Summary, PDF p. 2) and its v2.2 operative forms (§4.3: restrict model deployment and further scaling if the Required Safeguards showing cannot be made; §6.2: pause training until the ASL-3 Security Standard is implemented). Searched the text layer case-insensitively for pause, halt, stop, refrain, not train, not deploy, unless, until, restrict, delay, adequate, acceptable level, will not, cease, train and deploy. No passage stating a commitment not to train or deploy models unless adequate safeguards are implemented, or a commitment to pause training or deployment until such safeguards are in place, was found within the operative text. Hits examined and not counted: the Introduction (p. 3) describes in the past tense what the previous RSP committed to and discusses a hypothetical developer that pauses; §1 (p. 4) says Anthropic cannot unilaterally and unconditionally commit to its industry-wide recommendations; Appendix A (p. 16) commits to delay AI development and deployment only in the 'Anthropic in the lead' and 'Competitors have strong safety measures' scenarios and not necessarily under 'General upleveling' (proposed separately as rsp-competitor-lead-delay); wording about maintaining a commitment not to train or deploy without adequate safeguards occurs only in the reproduced changelog entry for RSP v2.0 (October 15, 2024; p. 17), which describes that earlier update. The conclusion is bounded by that scope and method.
claims.qualification: A recorded absence within the stated scope: not a claim that the provision was deleted, and not a statement about practice or intent.

claims.subject: california-sb-53

object.value: No materially false or misleading statements about framework implementation or compliance

claims.statement: SB 53 prohibits a large frontier developer from making a materially false or misleading statement about its implementation of, or compliance with, its frontier AI framework. It also prohibits any frontier developer from making a materially false or misleading statement about catastrophic risk from its frontier models or about its management of catastrophic risk. The prohibition does not apply to a statement made in good faith that was reasonable under the circumstances.

time.note: Provision as stated in the chaptered text published and approved on 2025-09-29; the added sections took effect on 2026-01-01. Text as chaptered on 2025-09-29; the Governor approved it and it was filed with the Secretary of State that day. claims.qualification: What the enacted text states, quoted from the chaptered expression. It is not evidence that the statute applies to any named developer, or of compliance, enforcement or effect. Subdivision (e)(1)(B) concerns statements about a large frontier developer's implementation of, or compliance with, its own frontier AI framework. Subdivision (e)(1)(A) concerns statements by any frontier developer about catastrophic risk from its frontier models or its management of catastrophic risk. Two questions are listed as stops and not resolved here because they need legal interpretation. The first is whether subdivision (e) reaches any named developer's published statement, for example the sentence asserting TFAIA compliance in xAI's December 2025 FAIF (record faif-2026-compliance-sentence). The second is whether that developer is a large frontier developer. A statement in violation of subdivision (e) is one of the grounds on which § 22757.15(a) makes a large frontier developer subject to a civil penalty. This record states what the statute requires. It says nothing about any developer's compliance.
